Which recommendation to adopt? The primary recommendation I'd adopt is "defer-parameter-change" — no controller parameter change justified. That's the core disposition: adopt deferring parameter changes. Actually let me think about the semantics: disposition "adopt" means I adopt the recommendation. The recommendation itself has action "defer". So adopting means I agree with deferring the parameter change. That seems right.

Alternatively adopt "defer-further-numerical-checks" since the allowance is spent. Hmm. But the most substantive final decision is: no configuration/parameter change is justified (adopt the defer-parameter-change recommendation), and finish.

Key: adopt the deferral of parameter/weight/horizon changes. The executed probe (update 30, t=0.30 s, model.gvs@1.0.0, 0.01 s horizon, implicit Euler 0.002 s, advisory_only=true) is the only authorized check and it is spent. It shows: from the same saved projected state, the recorded-applied rollout's projected tip speed rises 0.78274 → 1.26720 m/s over 10 ms (away from the 0.02 m/s scale, f0f6bbb27ee11), while the instantaneous braking-box rollout reverses tip-velocity direction at t=0.004 s and accumulates 0.00621 m total displacement (f8f871c47f799) versus the recorded rollout's 0.00867 m by t=0.008 s (f30cd065cbec9). It cannot arbitrate among objective weighting, seed/shallow-iterate plan selection, effective-horizon effects and projected-GVS-versus-backend model mismatch, and cannot explain the full settling miss (late_max_speed 1.581 vs 0.02 m/s, late_max_error 0.05814 vs 0.01 m, both f71bc2d719073/f29c08d890e75). So no parameter, weight, or horizon change is justified, and physical improvement was not evaluated. Other declared coverage gaps remain unread: backend motion before ~0.30 s, one-step predictions for updates 0-18, saved projected states other than update 30; historical full plans not retained; closed-loop replay/causal attribution unavailable.

Also disposition candidate: adopt. next_action: finish.

But wait — should I choose "defer-further-numerical-checks" instead? Both are defensible. The most salient final disposition is no configuration change. I'll go with "defer-parameter-change" as the primary recommendation and note in reasoning that this entails no further checks (allowance spent) and coverage gaps stay open. Actually the reasoning can note that I also concur with the other two recommendations.

Hmm, but adopting one recommendation while the field is singular... I'll set recommendation_id to "defer-parameter-change".

Let me keep reasoning moderately concise but complete. English.

One more consideration: "Adoption alone executes nothing." and "Recommendation disposition and next action are independent; finish ends the workflow." So adopt + finish is fine.

Also "Physical improvement was not evaluated." mention.

Length: aim ~250-400 words. Include handles.

Note "final_speed_change_m_s" is the change over the horizon; row0 0.48446 > 0 — speed increased. Row1 0.27210 — also positive but with direction reversal mid-way. I'll describe carefully: "total speed change over 0.01 s".

Actually row1 final speed is 1.05483 m/s (fa0f760e58426), > initial 0.78274, so speed change +0.272. So neither ends below 0.02 m/s. Interesting: both end well above the settling scale. That is a good point — even the braking-box rollout ends at 1.05483 m/s projected, far above 0.02 m/s. That further supports that a 10 ms local probe can't explain the settling failure. I can mention: the braking-box rollout's projected endpoint speed is 1.05483 m/s (fa0f760e58426), still far above the 0.02 m/s scale, so neither row reaches the settling scale within the probe horizon.
